_about: The fans the crowd's parts are cut from (tools/prep_crowd.py makes assets/stadium/crowd_kit.glb from this). Every fan is one whole Tripo character; its head, torso (the outfit) and legs become parts that fit any other part of the same gender. `template` is the prompt, with `{who}` from the fan. `source` is the raw model, from the project root; a fan without one is skipped. `use` lists the parts of the fan that go into the kit. `yaw` turns the model to face -Y in Blender. `joints` overrides a joint prep_crowd.py found (names as printed after JOINTS; [x, y, z] with the height = 1, front = -Y, the fan's left = +X). `keys` overrides a colour it sampled (`skin`, `hair`, `shirt`, `pants`: [r, g, b] 0..1 as in the texture; `hair`: null for a bald head). `options` tunes how its texture is read: `chroma` (0.07: how far from a sampled colour a pixel may be and still count as it; lower when skin gets painted as shirt) and `luma` ([0.4, 1.8]: how much darker and brighter); `bare` ("wrist": from which joint out the arms are bare and nothing on them is the shirt; "elbow" for short sleeves on arms whose skin is near the shirt's colour). `beard` (true for a fan whose beard hangs below the chin, so that it goes with the head and not with the shirt; only if the hair is not the colour of the shirt). `budgets` gives a fan triangle budgets of its own (same shape as the `budgets` below; what it leaves out is as for everybody). A `placeholder` fan is used only while its gender has no other fan with a source. A fan with `only`: "head" is a model of a head by itself (with its neck), not a whole character: it is not cut, only put on the gender's neck, with what is below its neck line inside the torso. `neck` says where that line is (0.15: that far up the model, 0 its bottom and 1 its top), `size` how big the head is beside the average head of the whole fans (1.0), `shift` moves it ([x, y, z], with the height = 1; front is -y), on top of the gender's `head_shift`, which moves every head that came by itself (so that a new one lands where the others are). Its skin colour is read off its face (what is lighter there than its hair), so give `keys.skin` if its hair is fair; with `keys` "skin": null and "hair": null it keeps the colours of its own texture, the same on every fan. A fan with `only`: "torso" is a torso with its arms by itself, open at the neck and at the waist: its collar goes to the gender's neck and its hem to the waist (times `size`, moved by `shift`), its arms are found and bent like a whole fan's (`joints` overrides `shoulder.L`, `tip.L`, ...), and its colours are read as usual. A fan with `only`: "legs" is a pair of legs (trousers and shoes) by itself, open at the waist: it stands on the ground with its waistband at the gender's waist (`size`, `shift`), and its legs are found and bent like a whole fan's (`joints` overrides `crotch`, `hip.L`, `knee.L`, `ankle.L`, ...). A gender's `skeleton` is the skeleton its parts are fitted to (joints with the height = 1, the half width of the waist, and the middle and half size in x and y of the cut edges at the neck and the waist): it is used when the gender has no whole fan, and prep_crowd.py prints a new one (SKELETON) whenever it has. A gender's `far_head`, `far_torso` and `far_legs` name the fans whose head, torso and legs the plainest level gets (otherwise the first fan's).
template: a sports fan, {who}, standing upright in a T-pose with arms straight out to the sides and legs slightly apart, clean shaven, smooth skin, chunky stylized cartoon character, simple shapes, single isolated figure
